text: Genesis 6 sets a world corrupt all the way down beside one man who walked with God (6:9). The narrator gives no softened account of the corruption. Every imagination of the thoughts of the human heart "was only evil continually" (6:5), the earth "was filled with violence" (6:11), and Yahweh "was sorry that he had made man" (6:6). Noah receives no commission to reform any of this. His commission is to build. The narrator spends more words on the ark's specifications (6:14–16) than on the corruption that makes the ark necessary, because Noah builds to a measure he did not set. The ark exists as dimensions, length and breadth and height and the placement of door and window, before it exists as gopher wood. About Noah's own part the chapter records a single sentence: "Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he" (6:22). He is called righteous in 6:9, before he lifts a tool. In this chapter that righteousness becomes visible as obedience, which is Noah's willingness to build what God, who has looked upon the whole earth and seen it corrupt (6:12), says will be needed.
